title: Delhi High Court Flags Safety Concerns in India’s HPV Vaccine Rollout for Girls
excerpt: A Division Bench led by Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya issued notice to the Centre and ICMR after a PIL challenged the nationwide Gardasil vaccination programme, citing alleged adverse reactions and lack of informed consent.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Delhi High Court questions safety of HPV vaccine rollout for girls amid a PIL.
  • Chief Justice Upadhyaya demands adverse event data by July 29 hearing.
  • A 14-year-old girl reportedly suffered severe complications after receiving the vaccine.
  • India's HPV vaccination campaign launched in February 2026 aims to combat cervical cancer.
  • Cervical cancer claims approximately 80,000 lives annually in India.
  • The Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre and ICMR on a PIL challenging the nationwide HPV vaccine rollout under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
  • Chief Justice Upadhyaya called it a “very important issue” and directed the government to submit adverse event data by the next hearing on July 29.
  • The PIL cited a 14-year-old Tamil Nadu girl who allegedly developed severe neurological complications after receiving the Gardasil vaccine in March 2026.
  • India launched the HPV vaccination campaign in February 2026 targeting adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer, which kills approximately 80,000 Indian women annually.

The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Central government and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) on a Public Interest Litigation challenging the nationwide rollout of Merck’s Gardasil vaccine under the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), raising questions about the vaccine’s safety data and consent procedures in its administration to adolescent girls.

A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia agreed to examine the petition and directed the Union government to produce data on adverse events following HPV vaccination by the next hearing, scheduled for July 29.

“Mr Sharma, very important issue. Vaccination is a good scheme, but if there are some adverse consequences, we will have to be very cautious. Seek instructions from the Ministry.”

— Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Delhi High Court

What the Petition Claims

The PIL was filed by gynaecologist Dr Sujata Mittal and fitness influencer Jitendra Chauksey, represented by Senior Advocate Gyanendra Kumar. The petitioners argue that the nationwide rollout of the HPV vaccine is proceeding without conclusive studies on its efficacy and safety for the Indian population, and that the programme violates constitutional rights to bodily autonomy and informed consent under Articles 21 and 19.

> **"HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection worldwide, and high-risk strains are responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancers."**

Central to the petition is the case of a 14-year-old girl from Tamil Nadu who allegedly developed severe neurological symptoms — including paralysis-like weakness, loss of voice, inability to walk, and blurred vision — within days of receiving the HPV vaccine in March 2026. The PIL also references similar reported incidents from Gwalior and Bihar.

The petitioners further allege that frontline health workers, including ASHA workers, have been assigned enrolment targets that create undue pressure on young girls and their families. In many cases, according to the petition, the vaccine is being administered in schools without proper informed consent or prior parental approval.

A Contested History

India’s relationship with HPV vaccination has been fraught for over 15 years. The petition references the findings of the 72nd Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, which in 2013 flagged irregularities in clinical trials of Gardasil and Cervarix, including deviations from protocol and lapses in obtaining participants’ consent during a PATH-led demonstration project involving tribal girls in Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

The PIL also cited international litigation against Gardasil’s manufacturer, noting that Merck & Co. announced a settlement exceeding $50 million in more than 200 lawsuits alleging serious health complications following vaccination, according to Bar and Bench.

The WHO has endorsed HPV vaccination, and international scientific literature has broadly established its safety profile. India finally launched its nationwide HPV vaccination campaign on February 28, 2026, announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, after a delay of more than a decade attributed to regulatory controversies and vaccine hesitancy.

The Public Health Stakes

India records over 120,000 new cases of cervical cancer and approximately 80,000 deaths each year, according to published medical research — one of the highest burdens globally. HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection worldwide, and high-risk strains are responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancers. The vaccination programme targets 14-year-old girls with a single dose of Gardasil, procured through the Gavi alliance.

The Court emphasised that it was not questioning the government’s intentions. “The issue concerns all girl children, and we have to tread a very cautious path,” the Bench observed, while asking Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma to seek a briefing from the Ministry and the drug control organisation before the next hearing.

Diaspora Dimension

The case comes at a sensitive time for the Indian diaspora, many of whom have followed the HPV vaccine debate closely. In countries like the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia, HPV vaccination has been a routine part of adolescent healthcare for over a decade. Diaspora families visiting India or sending children to Indian schools may face uncertainty about the programme’s safety monitoring, while the court’s intervention could shape broader perceptions of India’s public health infrastructure.

Concerns Over HPV Vaccine Safety
›PIL filed by Dr. Sujata Mittal and Jitendra Chauksey.
›Allegations of severe neurological symptoms in a 14-year-old girl.
›Pressure on health workers to meet vaccination targets.
›Concerns over informed consent during vaccine administration.

What Comes Next

The matter is listed for further hearing on July 29. The Court has directed the government to produce adverse event data and has asked that officials from the health ministry and the drug control organisation brief the ASG before the next date. The outcome could influence the pace and scope of India’s HPV vaccination drive — a programme with the potential to prevent tens of thousands of cancer deaths annually, but one that must now satisfy judicial scrutiny on safety and consent.
